blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Magic: The Gathering’s Commander (MTG) format is about to become more accessible, thanks to the upcoming Foundations Commander Decks.

Cited by Wizards of the Coast (WotC) as the most popular tabletop format for Magic: The Gathering, Commander can be an intimidating place for newer players, especially with its massive card pool and countless ways to build a deck. The Foundations Commander Decks aim to provide a more straightforward entry point, with each deck led by a notable monocolored commander that comes with its own straightforward game plan.
This gives players an immediate way to jump into Commander while also offering a glimpse at how each color can be built and played.
Calling All Angels
Calling All Angels is the mono white Angel tribal deck led by Giada, Font of Hope.
The deck’s goal is to overwhelm the battlefield with an aerial army of Angels. The wide assortment of Angels cover the early and midgame, which can quickly build up board presence.
Giada helps to accelerate the strategy by making subsequent Angels bigger as they enter the battlefield.

While some of the deck’s heavier cards–such as Herald of Eternal Dawn and Reya Dawnbringer–can make the deck feel clunky during its development, getting its early ramp online can set the deck up for a strong mid-to-late game.
Keen Engineering
Keen Engineering is the mono blue artifact deck headed by Sai, Master Thopterist.
Rather than focusing on blue’s traditional instant-speed interaction and counterspells, the deck instead leans heavily into artifacts.
Sai can create a 1/1 Thopter whenever an artifact spell is cast, making the deck’s primary game plan to build a mechanical army and overwhelm the battlefield through numbers and card advantage.
At first glance, the list can seem clunky with cards like Broodstar, Thought Monitor and Graaz, Unstoppable Juggernaut.
However, the deck has various ways to cheat artifacts onto the battlefield or reduce their costs, helping it deploy its heavier threats much more efficiently than the initial list might suggest.
Additionally, one of the deck’s more interesting aspects is how it turns the excess Thopters into additional resources.

They can be used as fodder for card draw or eventually become a legitimate win condition themselves, especially with cards like Forsaken Monument and Master of Etherium helping empower the artifact army.
Wretched Ranks
Wretched Ranks is a mono black Zombie tribal deck headed by the necromancer Ghoulcaller Gisa.
Revolving heavily around the Zombie archetype, it follows the familiar game plan of overwhelming the battlefield with an ever growing undead horde, with Gisa adding more bodies to the army.
There’s not much to say about Wretched Ranks other than how well designed it is right from the get go.
Cards like Cryptbreaker and Midnight Reaper give the deck ways to turn its growing horde into additional value, allowing you to draw cards while continuing to build your army.
At the same time, cards like Endless Ranks of the Dead and Headless Rider ensure that the Zombies keep coming even after an opponent thinks they’ve finally cleared the board.
Reign of Dragons
Reign of Dragons is the mono red Dragon tribal deck headed by Lathliss, Dragon Queen.
Of the five decks in the Foundations Commander release, the red deck feels the most awkward, largely due to the nature of red itself.
A color that is normally associated with speed and aggression is slowed down significantly by the need to build up enough mana for its larger threats.

There are other tribes in red that could have been the focal point, such as Goblins or, in more recent releases, Dwarves, but given the nature of the product, Dragons feel like the most fitting choice.

Once the Dragons do arrive, however, the deck has some serious haymakers. Scourge of the Throne, Scourge of Valkas and Terror of Mount Velus can all turn a developed board into a game ending threat, with the latter being a finisher in its own right. The problem is getting to that point, as the turns leading up to your biggest Dragons can feel like an awkward affair.
Tramplesaurus Rex
The green deck, Tramplesaurus Rex, is helmed by Ghalta, Primal Hunger and revolves around Dinosaurs as its main theme.
More than just another Dinosaur tribal deck,Tramplesaurus Rex does a good job of showcasing what makes green tick in Magic.
Of all the decks in the release, Tramplesaurus Rex feels like the most complete representation of its color.

Green is all about ramp, power and generating as much value as possible, and this deck has all of that and more. It has a full suite of Elves that can help accelerate your mana and even includes a copy of Birds of Paradise.

It also maintains the green agenda of casting creatures with strong power and toughness for relatively low mana costs, with cards like Steel Leaf Champion and Gigantosaurus showing just how much power green can put onto the battlefield.
The deck even has ways to make green feel even more unfair, letting you play creatures at instant speed with Yeva, Nature’s Herald or giving them haste with Surrak and Goreclaw.
These additions help showcase the different ways green can turn its already impressive creatures into even bigger threats.

Are they worth picking up?
There’s never been a shortage of ways to experience Magic as MTG continues to venture into worlds like Middle Earth, space through A New Frontier, or the multiverse with Reality Fracture.

With the Foundations Commander decks specifically designed as an introduction to the format, players can pick a strategy that fits their interests without having to build a Commander deck from scratch.

At the end of the day, Magic will always be about The Gathering. Whether you want to command an army of Angels, Zombies, Dragons or Dinosaurs, or simply build a mechanical army of your own, these decks provide an easy way to get your feet firmly into Commander.
The decks are set to release on October 2, 2026.
